notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already used up, so nothing was looked up through a search engine. Pages were opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent, robots.txt first and one request at a time: the campaign websites, each county's, city's and school district's own site, the two state parties' sites and local party units' sites, and the news sites' own search pages where their robots.txt allows it (hometownsource.com, winonapost.com, grandrapidsmn.com, kaxe.org, eplocalnews.org, faribaultcountyregister.com). Some campaign addresses were tried by name (an address lookup only); none of the names that exist turned out to be a campaign site for this slice.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned by running the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) on a scratch copy of the database; each of the eight filed in this slice was then opened and read. Two more were found another way and read: Tara Killen's (the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates links it) and Tina Culbertson's (Eden Prairie Local News's story on the council candidates links it).

Bryan Lawrence filed no website. The 8th Congressional District Republicans' page "2026 Candidates" links lawrenceformn.com under "HD 27B - Bryan Lawrence"; the site itself showed this reader a bot check and was not opened, so the website finding rests on the party page alone and the second reader may want to open the site in a browser. The same listing is kept under party_support, a key other parts of this sweep also use for a party page that names a candidate without the word endorsed; it is not an endorsement.

Not read, and nothing worked around: mncourts.gov (it answers scripts 403, so there is no court page for the two judges); Yellow Medicine County's site (its robots.txt asks all scripts to stay out); Nobles County's site and lawrenceformn.com (each answers a script with a bot check); the Campaign Finance Board's candidate viewer and Wikipedia's search (robots.txt); the Worthington Globe and the Austin Daily Herald (their robots.txt turns Claude's reader away); sd67dfl.org (robots.txt); sd33mngop.com and the Scott County Republicans' endorsed-candidates page (403).

Republican endorsements: none could be recorded. mngop.com lists statewide nominees only; the Otter Tail County Republican Party lists Jeff Backer under "Our Republicans in public office", which is not a 2026 endorsement; the Isanti County and Mille Lacs County Republicans' pages name Bryan Lawrence only as a sitting representative.

Nonpartisan offices: the party pages that publish local support in these places were read (the Senate District 46 and 49 DFL, the Crow Wing County and Winona County DFL, the Carver County, Isanti County, Todd County and Crow Wing County Republicans, the 3rd District and Senate District 32 and 40 Republicans). None names a candidate of this slice in a nonpartisan race. The Senate District 49 DFL's "Local Candidates we support" names two other Eden Prairie council candidates, not Tina Culbertson.

Nothing was found for D.J. Bullerman, Braden Hoefert, Adam Miller, Brian Hendey, Sherie Wagner, Tai Tran, Bruce Nelson, Ed Shaw or Jennifer Frank beyond what they filed. The council, commission and board pages of East Bethel, Vadnais Heights, Mounds View, Savage, Owatonna, the Brainerd schools and the Orono schools show none of them in office today; Orono's own candidates page calls Jennifer Frank a "New Candidate" and lists no website for her. The Faribault County Register names a D.J. Bullerman only in his work as a deputy, which is a job and not a public office, so nothing is recorded. KAXE's election guide prints Ed Shaw's answers; they state no public office. The White Bear/Vadnais Heights Press's 2026 Voters' Guide (September 16, 2026) prints "Candidate Brian Hendey did not respond".
Ages printed in voters' guides (KAXE for Tara Killen and Ed Shaw, the Forest Lake Times for Curt Rebelein) were not turned into birth years: an age on election day fits two birth years.

Starting years: where a page gives only an election year or the current term ("Elected: 2022", "Term: January 2023 - December 2026", "Term expires 1/4/2027"), the 'from' is left empty or written 'elected 2022' and the page's own words are in the source. Scott Bruns's 2015 is Cass County's own "Term 2015 to 2026"; Mike Allen's 2023 is the county's own list of sheriffs; Curt Rebelein's 2023 and Luke Cardona's 2025 are each stated by a second source as well.

Christian Sean Wilton: the Judicial Branch's site could not be read, so the only sources are court reports in Sun Thisweek: one of May 19, 2017 that calls him a Scott County judge, and the paper's 2015 year in review (https://www.hometownsource.com/sun_thisweek/news/local/year-in-review-2015-apple-valley-sees-triumph-scandal-and-heartbreak/article_a36fc7bc-d869-5f85-a35a-a7bfa3ec2897.html), which calls him a judge in a Dakota County case. Scott and Dakota counties are both in the First Judicial District. The 2017 story's headline names a defendant, so the headline is left out of the source line. His first name is also kept out of the office and source wording, because the loader's guard words include it and would hold the finding back by mistake.

Ron Antony: the county's own site may not be read by scripts. The one page found is the board list of Area II Minnesota River Basin Projects, a joint powers board of nine counties whose directors and alternates are, by its own About page (https://www.area2.org/about), county commissioners. It is marked official for the second reader to judge.

Sarah Hueser's About page names two boards she serves on. Only the school district's community education advisory board is recorded; the other belongs to a church, which is not a public office and not something a card may show. Her site (a Wix site) let this reader open one page and then answered 429, Too Many Requests, for a long while; the home page and the About page were each read once, some time apart, and were not asked for again.
Every page cited here except Sarah Hueser's two was opened a second time at the end, and the words quoted from it were found on it again.

Matti Adam: the end year for Itasca County Attorney is the year the Governor appointed her to the bench (reported April 10 and 11, 2024); neither story gives the day she left that office or the year she first took it.

The University of Minnesota Libraries' Minnesota Historical Election Archive (official returns for federal, statewide and legislative offices) was checked by name for every candidate here who is not a sitting legislator. It lists only Dwayne Voegeli's 2024 primary. It also has a Bruce Nelson who ran for State Senate as a Republican in 2000 and 2002 in districts in another part of the state; nothing ties him to the Owatonna candidate, so nothing is taken. The birth dates the archive shows were not taken: it draws them from a records index.

hometownsource.com (the Sun, ABC and Forest Lake Times papers) asks the crawlers that gather training text to stay out, ClaudeBot among them, but not ordinary readers or this kit's reader; its stories were read one at a time with the kit's honest User-Agent, as other parts of this sweep read them. Where a site's robots.txt names Claude's own reader for people's requests (Claude-User), it was left alone.

Dwayne Voegeli: the Winona Post's stories also describe his work outside public office; none of that is recorded. Its February 18, 2026 story says he announced he would not run again for the Minnesota House, which is why the 2024 run is the only one under a party label here.

verifier_notes: Every address in the file was opened again on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, one at a time, and the words recorded were found on the page; three script-drawn pages (Proctor schools, District 916, lukeforfridley.com) carry their words in the page's own data, where they were read.

Wording about a website being 'the address filed with the Secretary of State', and about pages that were named without an address (the Crow Wing County DFL, the Otter Tail County Republicans, Eden Prairie Local News, the campaign-site mention of the District 916 seat), was taken out of the 'how' and 'source' lines: the verifier did not see them. Each website still stands on its own title and words.
Matti Adam: the end year for Itasca County Attorney was an inference from her appointment and is now blank; the story says only that she held the office in April 2024.

Bryan Lawrence: party_support was confirmed on the 8th Congressional District Republicans' page ("HD 27B - Bryan Lawrence" under District 27, linking lawrenceformn.com; the word endorsed does not appear). It is not an endorsement and is not one of the rules' keys; the loader should treat it as a listing only.

Christian Sean Wilton: both Sun Thisweek stories were opened; the 2017 one says "Scott County Judge Christian Wilton" and the 2015 review says "Judge Christian Wilton". Scott County is in the 1st Judicial District, the seat sought. The cited story's address carries a defendant's surname; the card should show the paper and date, not the address text.

Ron Antony: Area II's board page lists "Ron Antony - Alternate" under Yellow Medicine and its About page says the board is made of county commissioners; kept as recorded, with no years and no district.
